message.content:
Let \(X\) be the number of rolls that show a 6. Since each roll is independent and the probability of rolling a 6 is \(p=\frac16\), we have

\[
X \sim \text{Binomial}\left(n=5, p=\frac16\right)
\]

We want \(P(X \le 2)\):

\[
P(X \le 2)=P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2)
\]

Using the binomial formula:

\[
P(X=k)=\binom{5}{k}\left(\frac16\right)^k\left(\frac56\right)^{5-k}
\]

Compute each term:

\[
P(X=0)=\left(\frac56\right)^5=\frac{3125}{7776}
\]

\[
P(X=1)=\binom51\left(\frac16\right)\left(\frac56\right)^4
=5\cdot \frac{625}{7776}
=\frac{3125}{7776}
\]

\[
P(X=2)=\binom52\left(\frac16\right)^2\left(\frac56\right)^3
=10\cdot \frac{125}{7776}
=\frac{1250}{7776}
\]

So,

\[
P(X \le 2)=\frac{3125+3125+1250}{7776}
=\frac{7500}{7776}
=\frac{625}{648}
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{625}{648}}\).
